description: Save a reusable skill: a named instruction bundle that you or another agent can run later with run_skill (list_skill_templates shows a worked example). The skill is recorded as authored by an agent, and unless `visibility: "personal"` is passed it is created SHARED with the whole workspace (every member's AI can find and run it), so teammates' AI will follow its text as instructions. `visibility: "members"` (with `members`) shares with only the named people; `public` can be requested, but that only raises an approval a person must give in the app Inbox and it is never public until they do. [Full notes: get_started section "TOOL NOTES create_skill"]

description.description: One or two sentences on what it does. Max 500 chars.

examples.description: Worked input→output pairs. One good example does more than a paragraph of clarification. Max 20.

from_template.description: Template id from list_skill_templates, recorded as provenance.

instructions.description: The actual procedure, as numbered steps, read later by someone with NO memory of this session: it names the databases and fields explicitly and says what NOT to do (invent a price, send anything). Max 20000 chars.

members.description: With visibility `members`: who can see it, as user ids from list_members or exact names. On update this REPLACES the whole set, so adding or removing someone means sending the full new list (get_skill returns the current one). Everyone not named gets nothing, not even a hint the skill exists.

name.description: Short, specific name — how a person will pick it out of a list. Max 100 chars.

visibility.description: Who can see it: `shared` (the whole workspace; the default), `personal` (only the token owner), `members` (only the people in `members`, plus you), or `public` (anyone with a link). `public` is NOT applied by this call: it raises an approval that a PERSON must give in the app Inbox; until then the skill stays as it was.

when_to_use.description: The trigger, in the words someone would use when they need it — this is what a future agent matches against, so "when a lead lands and needs a first reply drafted" beats "for leads". Max 1000 chars.
